q: 201. The remuneration of members of dispute adjudication board is paid by
explain: The remuneration and expenses of the Dispute Adjudication Board (DAB) members are shared equally (50-50) between the contractor and the client (employer).

q: 202. A frequency distribution curve
options: having single lump is called unimodal curve
if symmetrical is called normal curve
if unsymmetrical is called skew curve
explain: All given statements are true: a single peak indicates a unimodal curve, symmetry defines a normal distribution, and asymmetry indicates skewness.

q: 203. The mean coincides with the node, if frequency distribution curve is
explain: In a perfectly symmetrical distribution curve, the central measures of tendency—Mean, Median, and Mode (node)—coincide at the center peak.

q: 204. If the height of the frequency-distribution underneath is equal to unity, then curve is known as
explain: A standard normal distribution curve is defined such that the total area underneath the curve is equal to unity (1.0).

q: 205. Restraint is a restriction having
explain: In network scheduling, a restraint can act as a time lag or lead, which translates into restrictions with either positive duration or negative duration.

q: 206. The first step for formulation of any contract is
explain: Contract formulation begins with inviting bids from the public or pre-qualified vendors through publishing the tender notice.

q: 207. The amount of money deposited while bidding a tender as a guarantee of the party's willingness of carry out the work is called
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or bid security is deposited along with the bid submission to prove the bidder's genuine intent to undertake the work.

q: 208. The amount of money deposited by successful bidder as a security for satisfactory performance is called
explain: Performance security is required from the selected bidder prior to signing the contract to ensure the satisfactory completion of the project.

q: 209. The object of technical drawing is
explain: Technical drawings provide dimensions and details necessary for estimate preparation, material take-offs, and resource procurement.

q: 210. The amount of money paid to the contractor by the client after the agreement and before the execution of work, is known as
explain: Mobilization advance is an advance payment made to the contractor after signing the agreement to help setup initial site operations and resources.

q: 211. The increase in price of materials during the construction is called
explain: Price escalation refers to the increase in the cost of construction materials, equipment, or labor over time due to inflation or market fluctuations.

q: 212. The main criteria for the selection of any contractor to perform any work are
explain: A contractor's evaluation is comprehensive, covering technical qualifications, financial capacity, machinery availability, and relevant project experience.

q: 213. If the completion time for a particular project is 6 weeks and its expected time is 8 weeks, then the slack time for the project is
explain: Slack time = Scheduled Completion Time - Expected Time = 6 weeks - 8 weeks = -2 weeks. Negative slack indicates a project running behind schedule.

q: 214. According to "Contract Act 2055" the number of classes of contractor are
explain: Contractors are categorized into 4 distinct classes (Class A, B, C, and D) based on their technical capacity and financial strength.

q: 215. Any event affecting the project should be claimed to client by the contractor within
explain: Standard conditions of contract (such as FIDIC) mandate that notice of any claim must be submitted by the contractor within 28 days of the event occurring.

q: 216. The types of format in which the records of labors are kept on daily basis for executing works is known as
explain: A muster roll is the official record used in construction works to register daily attendance and calculate wages for site laborers.

q: 217. Quality control is done by
explain: Quality control testing and enforcement on site are primarily monitored and supervised by the technical consultant representing the employer.

q: 218. Quality assurance presents
explain: Quality Assurance (QA) consists of systemic actions planned and performed by the contractor to assure that the executed work meets specified standards.

q: 219. Project maintenance is concerned with
options: maintenance of useful life of plant
to maximize the return on investment
explain: Project maintenance encompasses equipment upkeep, plant operational longevity, and asset management to maximize overall return on investment.

q: 220. Preventive maintenance is a types of
explain: Preventive maintenance is a proactive, planned maintenance strategy carried out systematically to prevent sudden equipment failure.

q: 221. The relation between contractor and client should be
explain: A healthy professional relation between the contractor and client requires clear, decisive actions paired with active technical co-operation.

q: 222. During excavation of earth work supports are necessarily required if the depth of excavation exceeds more than
explain: Standard site safety precautions require shoring or timbering supports whenever earthwork excavation depth exceeds 4 feet (approx. 1.2 m).

q: 223. Unsafe working condition in construction industry causes
explain: Hazardous and unsafe site conditions directly result in a wide spectrum of incidents, ranging from minor injuries to fatal workplace accidents.

q: 224. What are the causes of accidents?
explain: Accidents stem from physical hazards (faulty equipment), physiological factors (fatigue/illness), and psychological factors (lack of focus/stress).

q: 225. To reduce accident, beware in construction site it should be
options: to aware of personal using equipment
to use medicine while there is accident
explain: Accident mitigation requires continuous safety training, operational awareness regarding equipment, and immediate first-aid medical availability.

q: 226. In many project responsibility of safety is given to
explain: Under standard construction conditions of contract, the contractor is primarily responsible for maintaining site safety and providing protective measures.

q: 227. Who is responsible for accident occurring at site?
explain: The main contractor holds overall responsibility for managing site conditions, safety protocols, and any accidents occurring within the project site.

q: 228. Aggregate planning is planning for
explain: Aggregate planning focuses on managing overall production capacity, labor, and resource allocation for the entire project as a whole.

q: 229. Modular co-ordination of construction means proper
explain: Modular coordination involves standardized dimensional planning, design layout, and component execution for seamless assembly.

q: 230. The objective of technical planning is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
taking remedial action about bottle-neck in execution
explain: Technical planning encompasses technical specifications, resource procurement schedules, and proactively solving execution bottlenecks.

q: 231. For the execution of work in time, work plan is prepared by
explain: The contractor prepares the detailed work execution schedule (master plan/bar chart) to ensure completion within the contract deadline.

q: 232. Monitoring is done for the purpose to
explain: Monitoring is an ongoing management function to collect progress data, review performance critically, and ensure effective project execution.

q: 233. The process of studying the result/output of a project is known as
explain: Evaluation is the systematic assessment of a project's completed activities, outcomes, and overall impact against set objectives.

q: 234. Evaluation of work is done to get as well as reform the expected output. The types of evaluation which is done before the implementation is known as
explain: Ex-ante evaluation takes place before project implementation to assess feasibility and anticipated outcomes.

q: 235. Monitoring helps for evaluation while evaluation helps for
explain: Evaluation findings guide corrective operational actions, refine ongoing monitoring systems, and improve future project planning.

q: 236. Monitoring for project work is checked by
explain: Project monitoring systematically tracks technical quality, quality management procedures, and budget expenditures.

q: 237. Monitoring & supervision for quality control is done for
explain: Quality control supervision ensures structural strength requirements, adherence to material specifications, and minimizes operational delays.

q: 238. Which one is the basis of project?
explain: A project's success relies foundational control processes: planning initial steps, scheduling timeframes, and active site monitoring.

q: 239. If variation occurs, what happens
explain: A variation order can result in an addition (increasing cost/time) or an omission (decreasing overall scope/cost).

q: 240. In any project the works contracted with consultant and department. If drawings have been changed, how much authority of department head to give variation of ......percent of original contract amount in contract procedure? (Source:PPA2063(54))
explain: Under Public Procurement Act (PPA 2063, Section 54), the Department Head holds authority to approve variations up to 15% of the original contract price.

q: 241. The document giving the information about the tender, prequalification, contractor, construction, procurement of materials and services is called
explain: The Public Procurement Act (PPA) and Public Procurement Regulations (PPR) govern procurement procedures, prequalifications, and contracting rules in Nepal.

q: 242. The authority of Gazetted First Class to approve the variation amount upto-------of the original contract value. (Source: PPA2063(54))
explain: According to Section 54 of PPA 2063, a Gazetted First Class Officer (Project Chief/Chief Officer) can approve variations up to 10%.

q: 243. If the variation amount is more than 15% of the original contract value of sixty million, then approval of the variation of cost may be done by
explain: Variations exceeding standard threshold limits are escalated up to the Department Head or Council of Ministers as designated by PPA regulations.

q: 244. Due to alteration of any component of the project the cost of original contract value
explain: Depending on whether the scope alteration involves additions, substitutions, or reductions, the contract cost may increase, decrease, or remain net constant.

q: 245. Due to alteration of any component of the project the duration of project
explain: Design alterations can lead to extended project deadlines, reduced completion windows, or no net change in the critical path duration.

q: 246. Due to omission of any component of the project the cost of project
explain: Omission of a work item directly removes itemized bill quantities, reducing the net overall project cost.

q: 247. Due to omission of any component of the project the duration of project may be
explain: If omitted work lies on a non-critical path activity, the total duration of the project critical path may remain completely constant.

q: 248. The time below witch the duration can not be further reduced is known as
explain: Crash time is the minimum absolute time required to complete an activity by expediting all available resources.

q: 249. The cost corresponding to crash time is
explain: Crashing increases direct resource costs to maximum, shortens duration (minimizing overhead indirect costs), resulting in a elevated direct/total cost scenario.

q: 250. The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is
explain: The optimal project duration occurs at an optimistic equilibrium point where the sum of direct and indirect costs reaches its minimum total value.

q: 251. The time with which direct cost does not reduce with the increase in time is known as
explain: Normal time represents standard activity execution duration where direct costs are minimized; extending beyond normal time does not lower direct cost further.

q: 252. The cost corresponding to the completion of activity within normal time is
explain: Normal cost is the lowest direct expenditure required to perform an activity under standard working conditions and normal duration.

q: 253. The direct cost of a project with respect to normal time is
explain: At normal duration, direct costs (labor, equipment, materials) are at their absolute minimum since no premium or overtime crashing expenditure is incurred.

q: 254. The reduction in project time normally results in
options: decreasing the direct cost and increasing indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and decreasing the indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
decreasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
explain: Compressing schedule duration requires additional resource deployment (raising direct cost) while reducing overhead time-dependent expenses (lowering indirect cost).

q: 255. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: Combining decreasing indirect costs and increasing direct costs yields a distinct U-shaped total cost curve with a clear minimum cost point.

q: 256. Assuming that the cost varies with time, the cost - slope is defined as
options: \frac{\text{crash cost - normal cost}}{\text{normal time - crash time}}
explain: Cost Slope represents the extra direct cost per unit time saved: $\text{Cost Slope} = \frac{\text{Crash Cost} - \text{Normal Cost}}{\text{Normal Time} - \text{Crash Time}}$.

q: 257. Direct cost of a project is due to
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages of labor
explain: Direct costs are expenses directly tied to executing tasks, such as material purchases, field equipment, and direct labor wages.

q: 258. Indirect cost of the project
options: decreases up to optimum duration and then increase with duration
explain: Indirect costs (site administration, overheads, security) compound over time, meaning longer project duration increases total indirect cost.

q: 259. Total project cost
options: initially reduces with time and then increases with further increases
explain: Starting from crash time, extending duration lowers high direct costs faster than indirect costs rise, creating an initial total cost drop until the optimum duration is reached.

q: 260. The reduction in project time normally results in
options: decreasing the direct cost and increasing indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and decreasing the indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
decreasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
explain: Reducing time increases direct costs (due to overtime/extra crews) and reduces indirect costs (due to shorter overhead exposure).

q: 261. In a time-cost optimization using CPM the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: To minimize cost expenditure when crashing a network, critical path activities with the lowest (least) cost slope are compressed first.

q: 262. Contractor's prequalification is required for project cost above (Source: PPR2064(3))
explain: Under Public Procurement Regulations (PPR 2064, Rule 3), mandatory pre-qualification is specified for large projects exceeding threshold values.

q: 263. Construction activities at site are directly associated with the management of
explain: Field management integrates control over basic resources: Manpower, Machinery, and Materials (the 3 Ms of construction management).

q: 264. The various types of contract are
explain: Standard public and private procurement methods include lump-sum, unit rate (item rate), and turnkey (EPC) delivery contracts.

q: 265. Mediation shall include the individuals involved in the dispute except
explain: Mediation is an informal dispute resolution process between employer, contractor, and neutral mediator; formal legal representation (attorneys) is generally excluded.

q: 266. The purpose of preparing job-layout for a construction project is:
options: reduction in wastage and deterioration of materials
higher productivity from labour and machinery
explain: A proper site job-layout minimizes material handling, reduces waste, optimizes machine placement, and boosts overall site productivity.

q: 267. Systematic reporting of work progress is the main objective of
explain: Flow process charts record operational steps, movements, and progress delays systematically across a production chain.

q: 268. Duty of obligation to satisfactorily perform a task that one must fulfill, and which has a consequent penalty for failure is:
explain: Responsibility defines an individual's obligation to carry out assigned duties with accountability for the outcome.

q: 269. An offer in writing to execute some specified civil works at certain rates within a fixed time under certaion conditions of contract is called:
explain: A bid (or tender submission) is a formal written offer submitted by a contractor detailing terms, rates, and timeframe to perform specified work.

q: 270. The report prepared at the end of finishing a construction job is called:
explain: A completion report is compiled after project closeout documenting finalized quantities, standard compliance, final costs, and hand-over details.

q: 271. Which of the following column is left blank in Bidding documentary by the employing agency?
explain: In Bill of Quantities (BOQ) tender documents, the employer supplies descriptions, units, and estimated quantities while leaving the unit rates blank for bidders to quote.

q: 272. As per Public Procurement Act/Regulation minimum time required for tender notice is :
explain: For national competitive bidding in Nepal under PPR regulations, standard public notice advertisement duration is minimum 30 days (or 45 days for international tenders).

q: 273. Which of the following is a primary process for procurement of goods and services from a competitive market?
explain: Bidding is the primary competitive mechanism used by public bodies to obtain optimal market prices for construction services and goods.

q: 274. An agreement between two parties or more to do or not to do any work is known as:
explain: By legal definition, a contract is an agreement enforceable by law between two or more parties creating mutual obligations.

q: 275. A written offer submitted by contractors to execute certain work at certain rates within a fixed time is called:
explain: A tender is an official written invitation response offering to perform construction works under stated rates and schedules.

q: 276. The document announcing to prospective bidders that the owner is ready to receive the bids is called:
explain: An Invitation for Bids (IFB) or Notice to Bidders publicly notifies qualified contractors that an employer is accepting bids for a project.

q: 277. Acquisition of land for any construction should be perfomed :
explain: To prevent site possession disputes and contract delays, land acquisition and right-of-way clearances must be secured prior to issuing tender notices.

q: 278. All measurement should be recorded in a :
explain: The Measurement Book (MB) is the official accounting document used to record all field work dimensions for preparing contractor interim and final bills.

q: 279. The time between ordering of the goods or materials and receiving and placing them into use at the point of need is called:
explain: Lead time is the total latency time elapsed between placing a purchase order and receiving delivery of materials at site.

q: 280. According to the Public Procurement Regulation, 2064, who approves the prequalification criteria? (Source:PPR2064(33))
explain: As mandated by PPR Rule 33, prequalification evaluation criteria and documentation require approval from the Head of Department.

q: 281. The supplementary specification prepared and applied if the standard specification does not cover the requirement of works under a contract is called:
explain: When general or standard specifications fall short for unique requirements, performance or special technical specifications are appended.

q: 282. The purpose of bid evaluation is to determine:
explain: Public procurement laws mandate selecting the lowest evaluated substantially responsive bid that meets technical and financial criteria.

q: 283. Which of the following is not Bid document?
explain: The Letter of Acceptance (LOA) is issued after evaluation during award stage; it is not a part of the original issued bidding documents.

q: 284. Which of the following is not a reason for establishing good occupational health and safety standard?
explain: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) standards are driven by moral responsibilities, legal compliance, and economic benefits—not religious considerations.

q: 285. The technique used for the management and development of Polaris Missile in American Navy Force is
explain: Program Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT) was specifically developed in 1958 by the US Navy for managing the Polaris Missile project.

q: 286. An EPC contract means:
explain: EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement, and Construction—a form of turnkey agreement where one contractor handles total delivery.

q: 287. The chart which gives an estimate about the amount of materials handling between various work stations is known as:
explain: A travel chart is a tabular matrix used to record and analyze quantitative volume of material transport between operational workstations.

q: 288. One of the tools for monitoring and evaluation of projects is:
explain: The Logical Framework Approach (LFA / LogFrame) is a standard methodology used for project planning, monitoring performance, and impact evaluation.

q: 289. For a safe working environment in the working site "Tool Box Talk" is conducted
options: at the end of day's work
explain: A Toolbox Talk is a brief safety meeting conducted on site right before commencing daily work tasks to discuss potential hazards.

q: 290. The money of the contractor retained by the department during payments is called:
explain: Retention money (usually 5% of interim bills) is deducted by the client to safeguard against defects during the defect liability period.

q: 291. Procurement of service means
explain: In public procurement rules, procurement of services specifically covers engaging consulting services, technical advisory, or study firms.

q: 292. Construction management involves :
explain: Construction management oversees site earthworks, heavy machinery operations, and workforce coordination.

q: 293. Construction activities at site are associated with the management of:
explain: Site construction processes center on organizing resource allocations across labor, construction materials, and heavy machinery.

q: 294. The purposes of preparing job-layout for a construction project is:
options: reduction in wastage & deterioration of materials
explain: As marked per answer key key[cite: 1], proper site storage layouts prioritize protecting material stockpiles from damage and waste.

q: 295. Earnest money is a ........ towards the execution of a publicly tender government contract.
explain: Earnest money is a security deposit made to guarantee bid commitment during public tender procedures.

q: 296. Quality control is done by using the method of
explain: Day-to-day quality control relies on direct inspection and technical supervision of ongoing work operations.

q: 297. Mile stones are
explain: In project scheduling, milestone events mark major progress points, key stage completions, or the initiation of major activity phases.

q: 298. The personnel involved in a project are provided safety measures for
explain: Safety provisions reduce site injuries, prevent fatalities, and create a secure workplace environment that improves worker morale and output.

q: 299. A turn key contract is offered for
explain: Turnkey contracts assign complete single-point responsibility covering conceptual planning, architectural design, procurement, and full construction.

q: 300. A variation order is issued to an contractor by the authorized personnel of the client when
options: it becomes necessary to change design and drawing
the quantity of items given in the contract document is to be charged
new items of work are required to be added
explain: A variation order covers alterations to original design drawings, quantity deviations from initial estimates, or introducing unanticipated extra items.

q: 301. The earned value technique in construction management is also known as
explain: Earned Value Analysis tracks baseline expenditure and performance over time, which is visually represented using cumulative S-curves.

q: 302. Amicable settlement means
explain: Amicable settlement involves resolving contract disputes through direct mutual negotiation and consensus between both parties without litigation.

q: 303. Codes used in Nepal for building construction/design is:
explain: Building design and structural safety in Nepal are primarily governed by the mandatory National Building Code (NBC) standards.

q: 304. A contractor can start the construction works following the receipts of
explain: Physical site execution officially commences after the client issues the formal Notice to Proceed (or Commencement Letter).

q: 305. Force majeure in contract is:
options: occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure covers unforeseeable extraordinary events beyond reasonable control (such as natural disasters or war) that prevent contract fulfillment.
